full_judgment:
3. The suit was filed stating, inter alia, that the land in suit belonged to Manada Chandra Ghosh. He borrowed Tk. 1,000/- from Nagesh Chandra Ghosh and as security Manada Chandra Ghosh executed 2 kabalas on August 1, 1962 and August 3, 1962 in favour of Nagesh Chandra Ghosh and on August 14, 1962 Nagesh Chandra Ghosh executed and registered an Ekrarnama in favour of Manada Chandra Ghosh to the effect that if the borrowed money is returned within two years, Nagesh Chandra Ghosh would reconvey the land of the aforementioned kabalas, that Manada Chandra Ghosh paid back the loan amount to Nagesh Chandra Ghosh and he executed a deed of re-conveyance on July 14, 1964 but the deed of re-conveyance could not be registered because of the provision of Ordinance No. 1 of 1964, that on execution of the deed of re-conveyance possession of the land in suit was surrendered by Nagesh chandra Ghosh to Manada Chandra Ghosh and he since the date of deed of re-conveyance possessed the land on payment of rent to the Government, that Manada Chandra Ghosh possessed the land to the knowledge of every body including Nagesh Chandra Ghosh, that Manada Chandra Ghosh died leaving son by name Madan Chandra Ghosh and wife Parul Bala and they possessed the land in suit, that Madan Chandra Ghosh and Parul Bala sold the land in suit to the plaintiff by the kabala dated January 31, 1985 and made over possession of the land so sold and the plaintiffs are in possession of the land since their purchase, that after purchase when the plaintiffs took steps for mutation of their names it was noticed that defendant No.1 illegally mutated his name in respect of the part of the land in suit and the plaintiffs as against the mutation filed objection and the same was allowed, that thereafter plaintiffs came to know that defendant No.1 in collusion with the defendant No.2 obtained two kabalas dated March 17, 1983 and March 28, 1983 in respect of the land in suit, that plaintiffs further came to know that defendant No.3 executed a kabala in favour of defendant No.5 on December 13, 1989 in respect of the land in suit, that after re-conveyance predecessor of plaintiffs vendor possessed the land in suit in assertion of his right and after him plaintiffs' vendors possessed the land in question of their right and adversely against all including the defendants over the statutory period of limitation prior to the selling of the land to the plaintiffs and plaintiffs' vendor inducted the plaintiffs into possession of land in suit, that the plaintiffs have acquired title in the land in suit by purchase as well as by adverse possession, that as the kabalas of the defendant Nos.1 and 5 have created cloud on the title of the plaintiffs, they are constrained to file the suit. 

 7. We have heard the learned Advocate and perused the materials in the petition for leave to appeal. From the judgment of the High Court Division as well as of the Courts below it is seen that possession of the plaintiffs and prior to the their vendors for more than statutory period of limitation for acquiring title has been established by documentary as well as by oral evidence.
